newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia Orchestra strikes on eve of season.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia Orchestra strikes on eve of season.

text.p: The 103 musicians of the Philadelphia Orchestra voted on Sunday to strike over a contract dispute, forcing cancellation of Tuesday's season-opening gala.
Musicians planned to begin picketing the famed Academy of Music on Monday morning in the first strike by the orchestra players in 30 years.
Bob Bedard, spokesman for the musicians, said on Sunday "management has already called to seek a resumption of negotiations".

The key issue is the fate of a $6,000 annual "electronic media guarantee," a share of orchestra's income from radio performances and recordings. The orchestra currently has neither a recording contract nor regular broadcasts and management's final offer included only a one-year guarantee of $2,000.
The offer included a 10 percent raise in the $72,000 base salary over three years, according to orchestra board chairman Peter Benoliel.
Bedard said: "This is not about money. The musicians are asking the orchestra to protect its own future."

He said that without a record contract and regular broadcasts the orchestra would lose an entire generation of new listeners and had previously accused management of "failing to guarantee that this will not become a second rate orchestra."
The orchestra has cancelled its schedule through Sept. 24, advising ticket holders to trade them in for cash or hold them for a future concert.
